newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE Euroswiss tumbles, chart view darkens.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE Euroswiss tumbles, chart view darkens.

text.p: Euroswiss futures on LIFFE fell sharply again on Wednesday following a steep decline on Tuesday, sending out gloomy technical signals, analysts said.
"Yesterday it broke down out of a triangle formation," said Francoise Skelley, head of global trading technical analysis at Credit Suisse First Boston in London.
She said the first target of that pattern was a 97.90-95 band, the lower level of which might hold for a short-term bounce. But that would not alleviate pressure further out.
June Euroswiss on LIFFE at 0909 GMT were at 97.99, 0.08 below the prior close, and down from a 98.15 high on Tuesday.
The market touched a key 97.90 low on January 7.

"Overall pressure will remain on the downside looking for 97.84-83," Skelley said, adding that the overall target on the downside was the 97.55-50 area. The June futures touched a 97.51 low on November 5, 1996, which preceded a three-and-a-half month rally to the 98.38 area, a high touched several times in February.
"The break from the triangle is going to cause an acceleration," Skelley said.
Some dealers attributed the Euroswiss weakness to speculation of an increase in Swiss interest rates.

This followed a statement by Swiss National Bank chairman Hans Meyer on Tuesday to a parliamentary committee which included the comment, "Interest rates may rise slightly as the consequence of an upturn.
But an SNB spokesman on Wednesday said the economic situation had not changed and monetary policy remained generous.

"We have always emphasised that we would first go to a less expansive monetary policy, when the economy revives again. We would only tighten the monetary reins when the economic recovery is underway," the spokesman said.
An analyst at a European bank in London said a targeted move up to 98.25 was put on hold. He added the 97.90s area represented a 50 percent retracement of the main November to February upmove.
In the Euroswiss options market, dealers said there was no volume going through.
